description.narrative: The Montreal Protocol Multilateral Fund (MPMF) is dedicated to reversing the deterioration of the Earth's ozone layer. It was established in 1991 to assist developing countries meet their Montreal Protocol commitments. It is managed by an Executive Committee with equal membership from developed and developing countries. The Fund is replenished on a three-year basis with contributions determined according to the United Nations Scale of Assessment.

title.narrative: Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: Since 1991, the Multilateral Fund for the Implementation of the Montreal Protocol has supported developing countries to phase-out their use of ozone depleting chemicals to help restore the ozone layer. With the adoption of the Kigali Amendment in 2016, the Multilateral Fund is now starting to assist developing countries to phase-down their use of hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), which are high global warming greenhouse gas substitutes for the ozone depleting chemicals. In 2023, the Fund approved 101 HFC related projects, including HFC phase-down plans for 24 countries to assist them to meet their first reduction step of 10% of their HFC baseline by 2029. In addition to assisting countries to reduce their HFC use, the Fund is also looking to assist countries to improve the energy efficiency of their HFC phase-down activities to increase even further the climate benefit of the HFC phase-down.
